subject: geography
title: Landforms and erosion
objective: Describe how water, ice, and wind shape the land.

lesson.opening: Landscapes are built by uplift and carved by erosion. The shape of a valley or coast records which process did the work.

sections.heading: Weathering and erosion
sections.body: Weathering breaks rock in place; erosion carries the pieces away. Water, ice, wind, and gravity are the main movers.

sections.heading: Rivers and coasts
sections.body: Rivers cut valleys, carry sediment, and build deltas at their mouths. Waves erode headlands and deposit sand to form beaches and spits.

sections.heading: Ice and wind
sections.body: Glaciers carve U-shaped valleys and leave ridges of debris. Wind builds dunes in dry regions.

Pick one landform and explain the process that created it.
activities.context: Water, ice, and wind each leave a recognizable signature on the land.
